question: Find the LCM of (2)/(5), (3)/(5) and (1)/(2).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of fractions = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)

Numerators: 2, 3, 1 → LCM = 6

Denominators: 5, 5, 2 → HCF = 1

Required LCM = 6 ÷ 1 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Fractions: 2/5, 3/5, 1/2

Formula used: LCM of Fractions = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)

 
 LCM of Numerators (2, 3, 1) = 6
 
• 
 
 HCF of Denominators (5, 5, 2) = 1

⇒ Identify the numerators: 2, 3, and 1.

⇒ Multiples of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, ...

⇒ Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, ...

⇒ Multiples of 1: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ...

⇒ Least Common Multiple (LCM) of (2, 3, 1) = 6

⇒ Identify the denominators: 5, 5, and 2.

⇒ Factors of 5: 1, 5

⇒ Factors of 2: 1, 2

⇒ Highest Common Factor (HCF) of (5, 5, 2) = 1

⇒ LCM of Fractions = 6 ÷ 1 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

To find the Highest Common Factor of fractions, use the formula: HCF of Fractions = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators).

Simplest Form Requirement

Before applying LCM/HCF formulas, always ensure all given fractions are reduced to their lowest (simplest) terms.

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).</p
